rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sea-and-ink image is a metonymy for the inexhaustibility of God's knowledge, including answers to the three questions; it does not imply that God's words can run out.
rows.anchor: كناية عن عدم تناهي معلومات الله تعالى التي منها تلك المسائل الثلاث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause about bringing an equal sea is circumstantial, while لو is concessive: even the strongest imaginable extra supply would not defeat the statement; this is a second intensification.
rows.anchor: وجملة { ولو جئنا بمثله مددا } في موضع الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: مددا is an accusative specification that resolves the ambiguity of مثله: the added supply is another sea like it.
rows.anchor: المفسر للإبهام الذي في لفظ { بمثله }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage turns from God's limitless knowledge to the Messenger's human limits: he was not sent to report all past events or answer every question, and knows only what God teaches him.
rows.anchor: ولكنه بشر علمه كعلم البشر أوحى الله إليه بما شاء إبلاغه عباده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إنما أنا بشر مثلكم is an additional restrictive construction aimed at correcting the expectation that a messenger transcends humanity into knowledge of the unseen.
rows.anchor: فالحصر في قوله { إنما أنا بشر مثلكم } قصر الموصوف على الصفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: يوحى إلي is either an independent sentence or a second adjective for بشر.
rows.anchor: وجملة { يوحى إلي } مستأنفة ، أو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The open-hamza أنما combines مصدرية أن with the restriction of إنما; it restricts divinity to oneness without partners.
rows.anchor: و { أنما مفتوحة الهمزة أخت ( إنما ) المكسورة الهمزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional about hoping to meet the Lord is part of the revelation and teaches belief in resurrection and righteous deeds alongside God's oneness.
rows.anchor: وتفريع { فمن كان يرجو لقاء ربه } هو من جملة الموحى به إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording presents three foundations: monotheism as the root, then resurrection and good works; forbidding association confirms God's unity and returns the ending to the surah's opening warning.
rows.anchor: إذ جعل التوحيد أصلا لها وفرع عليه الأصلان الآخران

rows.speaker: أبو مريم
rows.claim: A report from Abu Maryam says the Prophet named his newborn daughter Maryam because that surah had been revealed that night.
rows.anchor: عن أبي بكر بن عبدالله بن أبي مريم الغساني عن أبيه عن جده أبي مريم قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Ashur doubts the naming report: the surah's inferred fourth year of revelation predates Abu Maryam's known Muslim period, so he does not consider the report acceptable.
rows.anchor: وليس أبو مريم هذا معدودا في المسلمين الأولين فلا أحسب الحديث المروي عنه مقبولا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas called the surah كهيعص; al-Bukhari likewise gives this name in most of the best manuscript copies, while al-Suyuti did not count it as having two names.
rows.anchor: وابن عباس سماها سورة { كهيعص ، وكذلك وقعت تسميتها

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority regard Maryam as Meccan; Muqatil alone is cited for the prostration verse being Medinan, a view Ibn Ashur rejects because it interrupts the preceding passage unless appended later, which he finds unlikely.
rows.anchor: وهي مكية عند الجمهور . وعن مقاتل

rows.speaker: السيوطي
rows.claim: Al-Suyuti mentions, without naming an authority, a view that verse 19:71 is Medinan.
rows.anchor: وذكر السيوطي في ( الإتقان ) قولا بأن قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah is forty-fourth in revelation order, after Fatir and before Ta-Ha; the account of Umar's conversion places it around year four, and its distinctive Mary-and-family narrative explains its name.
rows.anchor: نزلت بعد سورة فاطر وقبل سورة طه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah's distinctive purpose is to answer the Jews' offensive claims about Mary and her son by establishing the purity and holiness of the family of Imran.
rows.anchor: نزلت للرد على اليهود فيما اقترفوه من القول الشنيع في مريم وابنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its verse count is ninety-nine in the Medinan and Meccan enumerations, and ninety-eight in the Syrian and Kufan enumerations.
rows.anchor: وعدت آياتها في عدد أهل المدينة ومكة تسعا وتسعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening letters are names of letters written in their named forms; they are normally pronounced with a pause because they are independent letters or abbreviations.
rows.anchor: والأصل في النطق بهذه الحروف أن يكون كل حرف منها موقوفا عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Readers differ on the vowels and assimilation: Abu Amr, al-Kisai, and Abu Bakr from Asim incline ها; Nafi and Ibn Kathir have an intermediate vowel; Ibn Amir, Hamza, and al-Kisai incline يا; readers also differ on pronouncing or assimilating the دال of صاد.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو ، والكسائي ، وأبو بكر عن عاصم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He reviews conjectures that كهيعص abbreviates divine names, forms God's greatest name, or names the Quran, but says no dependable hadith supports them.
rows.anchor: وليس في ذلك حديث يعتمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ذكر opens the account as the predicate of an omitted هذا, meaning this is an account of your Lord's mercy; alternatively it is a raised verbal noun functioning as a command, with elevation signaling constancy.
rows.anchor: والتقدير : هذا ذكر رحمة ربك عبده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mercy mentioned is the answering of Zachariah's prayer, later made explicit in the birth announcement; describing the prayer as private does not praise secrecy.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالرحمة : استجابة دعائه ، كما سيصرح به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zachariah's declaration that his bones weakened and his head blazed gray prepares the urgent request for an heir: he is distressed and needs a successor, not seeking pleasure or prestige.
rows.anchor: وهي وما بعدها تمهيد للمقصود من الدعاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two reports of weakness and gray hair pragmatically plead for mercy, since Zachariah already knows their content; mentioning the bones implies weakness throughout the body because bones support it and are its strongest part.
rows.anchor: مستعملان مجازا في لازم الإخبار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: العظم is definite as a generic noun, extending the weakness to all his bones; اشتعل pictures spreading white hair as fire across black charcoal in an elaborate representational simile.
rows.anchor: تعريف الجنس دال على عموم العظام منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fire image is encoded through the verb اشتعل, while assigning it to the head signals that grayness has reached the scalp after usually covering the beard, marking advanced age.
rows.anchor: فشبه الشعر الأسود بفحم والشعر الأبيض بنار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Attributing اشتعل to the head is an unusual rational metaphor: شيبا specifies the gray hair, creating detail after generality and an elegant concise effect; al-Kashshaf and al-Miftah discuss its eloquence.
rows.anchor: لأن الاشتعال من صفات النار المشبه بها الشيب

rows.speaker: أبو بكر بن دريد
rows.claim: Ibn Duraid echoes the image of whitened hair spreading across dark hair like fire through charcoal; Ibn Ashur says the line likely became proverbial.
rows.anchor: واشتعل المبيض في مسوده مثل اشتعال النار في جزل الغضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gray hair is whiteness caused usually by aging-related loss of the material producing the original color, though illness can also whiten hair.
rows.anchor: ويعرض للشعر البياض بسبب نقصان المادة التي تعطي اللون الأصلي للشعر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In لم أكن بدعائك رب شقيا, the باء means accompaniment; denying misery indirectly affirms happiness, since misery is deprivation and the two have no ordinary middle state.
rows.anchor: والشقي : الذي أصابته الشقوة ، وهي ضد السعادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expression functions proverbially to say that God's answering of prayer brings happiness; the same wording at 19:48 and a Prophetic report about people remembering God express this meaning, as does an unnamed Islamic poet.
rows.anchor: ونظيره قوله تعالى في هذه السورة في قصة إبراهيم :

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra transmits a report from the Prophet quoting God: those who remember God are companions whose associates do not become wretched, meaning they become happy.
rows.anchor: وفي حديث أبي هريرة عن النبيء صلى الله عليه وسلمفيما يرويه عن ربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الموالي means agnates and the nearest kin; من ورائي means after Zachariah's death, with النابغة's verse illustrating وراء as after.
rows.anchor: العصبة وأقرب القرابة ، جمع مولى بمعنى الولي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: من ورائي is an adjective for الموالي or a circumstantial phrase, and means after my life.
rows.anchor: فإن الوراء يطلق ويراد به ما بعد الشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zachariah's wife was named Elizabeth, descended from Aaron, Moses' brother, and belonged to Levi.
rows.anchor: وامرأة زكرياء اسمها أليصابات من نسل هارون أخي موسى فهي من سبط لاوي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: عاقر is specifically a woman who cannot bear children, so it lacks a feminine marker; its verbal noun has two vowel variants, and كان marks infertility as established, explaining why she bore no child.
rows.anchor: والعاقر : الأنثى التي لا تلد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asking for a wali from God's special presence requests a gift beyond ordinary reproductive causes, a gracious miracle; لي and من لدنك both depend on هب, with لي advanced because the personal aim takes priority.
rows.anchor: دل على أنه سأل وليا غير جار أمره على المعتاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most readers have يرثني as an indicative adjective of وليا; Abu Amr and al-Kisai read it jussively as the result sought by Zachariah's prayer.
rows.anchor: قرأه الجمهور بالرفع على الصفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: آل يعقوب may mean the honored house of Israel, especially scripture-bearing scholars, as in references to the families of Abraham and Noah; family names in such contexts imply following the ancestor's way.
rows.anchor: كأنه قال : ويرث من آل إسرائيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The announced speech is elliptically introduced as God's words to Zachariah; تبشير is a promise of a gift, and اسمه يحيى is a report used as a command to name him Yahya.
rows.anchor: مقول قول محذوف دل عليه السياق عقب الدعاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A common interpretation takes سميّا as someone with the same name before Yahya; the name's novelty honors Zachariah and makes the child easier to distinguish and a model for later naming.
rows.anchor: والسمي فسروه بالموافق في الاسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Ashur instead prefers سميّا as one matching Yahya in descriptive qualities: no earlier prophet combined his childhood wisdom, chastity, miraculous parentage, role announcing Jesus, and novel name.
rows.anchor: وعندي : أن السمي هنا هو الموافق في الاسم الوصفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yahya's many distinctive merits do not prove he surpasses all prophets, since rank depends on the totality of merits; the maxim is that a special merit does not entail superiority.
rows.anchor: وهي لا تقتضي أنه أفضل الأنبياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zachariah's أنى is astonishment expressing gratitude, not doubt after asking for a son; alternatively he may have expected a child through another wife. The parallel passage is in Aal Imran.
rows.anchor: و { أنى } استفهام مستعمل في التعجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating that his wife is barren shows Zachariah thought her infertility was the cause; people wrongly overlooked male infertility when erection and ejaculation were present, though either partner can have causes of infertility.
rows.anchor: وهو يقتضي أن زكرياء كان يظن أن عدم الولادة بسبب عقر امرأته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: من in من الكبر is a figurative point of origin expressing cause; age means many years and brings reduced activity and bodily disorder.
rows.anchor: و { من } في قوله { من الكبر عتيا } للابتداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: عتيا is the object of بلغت; reaching old age is figurative arrival at its term, and the wording differs from Aal Imran, where age itself is the subject that has reached Zachariah.
rows.anchor: والبلوغ : مجاز في حلول الإبان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority's عتيا derives from a dry, hardened stick; its vowel and consonant changes avoid a cluster of heavy vowels, while the kasra distinguishes it from عتوّ meaning rebellion.
rows.anchor: والعتي بضم العين في قراءة الجمهور مصدر عتا العود إذا يبس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The answer is separated as direct dialogue and corrects Zachariah's astonishment; on one reading كذلك points to his age and his wife's infertility, which God decreed by creative command.
rows.anchor: أي كذلك الحال من كبرك وعقر امرأتك قدر ربك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: هو علي هين answers the question raised by the decree: creating a child is easy for God's immense power.
rows.anchor: فجملة { هو علي هين } استئناف بياني جوابا لسؤال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively كذلك refers to God's just-stated answer, whose clarity needs no further explanation; on this reading هو علي هين explains the rejection of astonishment and shifts from third-person قال ربك to God's first-person voice.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون المشار إليه بقوله { كذلك } هو القول المأخوذ من

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: وقد خلقتك is circumstantial: creating a child in an unusual situation is no more astonishing than God's earlier creation of Zachariah from nothing.
rows.anchor: فكما لا عجب من خلق الولد في الأحوال المألوفة كذلك لا عجب من خلق الولد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ولم تك شيئا means Zachariah did not exist before God created him.
rows.anchor: ومعنى { ولم تك شيئا } : لم تكن موجودا

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وخلف
rows.claim: Most readers recite وقد خلقتك with first-person singular; Hamza, al-Kisai, and Khalaf read وقد خلقناك with the majestic plural.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور { وقد خلقتك } بتاء المتكلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zachariah asks for a sign of when the promised pregnancy begins, since no date was set and fulfillment could be delayed; omitting the complement of آية hints at his wish for haste.
rows.anchor: أراد نصب علامة على وقوع الحمل بالغلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The inability to speak is a divinely given sign; a mere command to remain silent would not suit the role of a sign.
rows.anchor: ومعنى { ألا تكلم الناس } أن لا تقدر على الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Three nights here means the nights together with their days, corresponding to three days and nights in Aal Imran; سويا means complete, while an alternative makes it describe Zachariah as physically sound without a speech defect.
rows.anchor: فعلم أن المراد هنا ليال بأيامها وأن المراد في آل عمران أيام بلياليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zachariah likely leaves his private prayer place to lead the community prayer as their chief priest; خرج على قومه means he appeared among them, as in the account of Qarun.
rows.anchor: الظاهر أن المعنى أنه خرج على قومه ليصلي على عادته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A محراب is a room or enclosed place reserved for private worship; al-Hariri's phrase plays on the word.
rows.anchor: والمحراب : بيت أو محتجر يخصص للعبادة الخاصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here revelation means a gesture, such as signaling with the eyes; أن is explanatory because أوحى implies speech, and the gesture tells the people to glorify God morning and evening.
rows.anchor: والوحي : الإشارة بالعين أو بغيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command avoids people mistaking his inability to speak for a vow of silence and copying it; silence had been worship in earlier laws, as Mary's later vow also shows.
rows.anchor: وإنما أمرهم بالتسبيح لئلا يحسبوا أن زكرياء لما لم يكلمهم قد نذر صمتا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, they may be asked to praise God in gratitude for granting their prophet a son, or the command may be deliberately general until Zachariah's speech returns.
rows.anchor: أو أراد أن يسبحوا الله تسبيح شكر على أن وهب نبيئهم ابنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The words to Yahya are an omitted divine speech, marking the transition from his announcement to his prophethood; they are Quranic narration, not necessarily words spoken to Zachariah.
rows.anchor: والأظهر أن هذا من إخبار القرآن للأمة لا من حكاية ما قيل لزكرياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Book is the Torah; taking it means understanding and applying it, and taking it with قوة means firm resolve to follow it and lead the community in following it as Jewish practice was weakening.
rows.anchor: والكتاب : التوراة لا محالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الحكم can mean prophethood, as in other Quranic usage, or wisdom and understanding; Ibn Ashur finds childhood prophethood unlikely and reads صبيا as exceptional sound judgment and perception in boyhood.
rows.anchor: والمراد بها النبوءة ، كما تقدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yahya did receive prophethood well before forty; perhaps God hastened it because he intended Yahya to be martyred early in life.
rows.anchor: واتفق العلماء على أن يحيى أعطي النبوءة قبل بلوغ الأربعين سنة بكثير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: حنان means compassion; it is also an attribute of God, and the expression حنانيك means compassion upon compassion, showing Yahya's divinely bestowed quality exceeds ordinary human measure.
rows.anchor: والحنان : الشفقة . ومن صفات الله تعالى الحنان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: زكاة means purification of the soul from evil, as in the command to purify oneself, or it may mean blessing.
rows.anchor: والزكاة : زكاة النفس ونقاؤها من الخبائث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: تقي is an intensive form meaning devoted to avoiding what conflicts with religion; كان تقيا indicates this quality was firmly established.
rows.anchor: وجيء في وصفه بالتقوى بفعل { كان تقيا } للدلالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His dutifulness to his parents is likewise presented as established; البرور means honoring them and striving to obey, with the verbal-form adjective intensifying praise.
rows.anchor: والبرور : الإكرام والسعي في الطاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: جبار describes one who violates people's rights by force; عصي is intensive, but the emphasis falls on negation, meaning Yahya was not disobedient at all.
rows.anchor: أي لم يكن عاصيا بالمرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The greeting is attached to God's giving Yahya wisdom and addressed to Muslims, so they recognize his honor; it is God's praise and protection across his three life transitions.
rows.anchor: الأظهر أنه عطف على { وءاتيناه الحكم صبيا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: سلام is a greeting containing praise or a prayer for safety; here it is God's greeting and praise, comparable to the greeting from a merciful Lord and the later greeting of Jesus.
rows.anchor: فالمراد هنا سلام من الله عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Birth, death, and resurrection represent the beginning of worldly life, departure, and entry into the next life; اليوم means the time of each event, and the present tense vividly evokes Yahya's death, whose killing the Quran only summarizes.
rows.anchor: وهذه الأحوال الثلاثة المذكورة هنا أحوال ابتداء أطوار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: اذكر في الكتاب مريم continues the preceding story by adding Mary's narrative to Zachariah's; the construction remains apt even if ذكر رحمة ربك is a verbal noun standing in for its verb.
rows.anchor: جملة { واذكر في الكتاب مريم } عطف على جملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ذكر means recite Mary's account, and the opening draws interest; في الكتاب clarifies that the account is in the Quran, not merely a separate statement of the Prophet, and helps establish the intended sense of other commands to remember.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالذكر : التلاوة ، أي اتل خبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إذ can attach to اذكر through its sense of narrating a story, or serve as a time noun appositional to Maryam, as in the earlier Zachariah account.
rows.anchor: و { إذ ظرف متعلق باذكر } باعتبار تضمنه معنى القصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: انتبذت means withdrawing into solitude; مكانا is either an object because the verb includes the sense of dwelling or a locative because the place is indefinite, and its kind is left unspecified since it does not matter to the story.
rows.anchor: والانتباذ : الانفراد والاعتزال ، لأن النبذ : الإبعاد والطرح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The place is called eastern to allude to Christians' eastward prayer orientation after Mary's pregnancy near sunrise's direction; Ibn Abbas linked the custom to this verse, but Ibn Ashur says it was not divinely prescribed, and the detail also fits the verse-ending rhythm.
rows.anchor: فللتنبيه على أصل اتخاذ النصارى الشرق قبلة لصلواتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary may have made the screen to bathe or to comb her hair.
rows.anchor: قيل : إنها احتجبت لتغتسل وقيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Spirit is an angel, inferred from God's sending him and the divine possessive; his human appearance was an assumed likeness, not his original form, and بشر is a circumstantial simile meaning a complete human form.
rows.anchor: والروح : الملك ، لأن تعليق الإرسال به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angel appeared fully formed to match the perfection of his actual nature; Mary thought a man had hidden there to seduce her, so her immediate appeal to God demonstrates her chastity.
rows.anchor: وإنما تمثل لها كذلك للتناسب بين كمال الحقيقة وكمال الصورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary's declarative refuge is emphatic: she makes God her protection and invokes الرحمن because she seeks mercy against the man she fears; the conditional إن كنت تقيا doubts his piety to stir fear of God.
rows.anchor: وذكرها صفة ( الرحمن ) دون غيرها من صفات الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إنما أنا رسول ربك is an additional restriction meaning the angel is no human, correcting Mary's assumption.
rows.anchor: والقصر في قوله : { إنما أنا رسول ربك } قصر إضافي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most readers have the angel say لأهب, figuratively assigning the gift to himself as its cause; Abu Amr and Warsh read ليهب, explicitly making God the giver, and Ibn Ashur explains the written alif and softened hamza.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور { لأهب } بهمزة المتكلم بعد لام العلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary's exchange with the angel tries to turn him from his mission because she knows he is sent by God but cannot bear the social harm; Ibn Ashur compares her appeal with Abraham's and Muhammad's intercession.
rows.anchor: ومحاورتها الملك محاولة قصدت بها صرفه عما جاء لأجله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لم يمسسني بشر means no husband had consummated marriage with her: she was betrothed to Yusuf the carpenter, so an unexplained pregnancy would expose her to accusation.
rows.anchor: لأنها كانت مخطوبة ومراكنة ليوسف النجار ولكنه لم يبن بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لم أك بغيا is not redundant: it denies that she had been a prostitute before and implies she will not accept that shame later; her past innocence is evidence against the accusation by continuity.
rows.anchor: فالكلام كناية عن التنزه عن الوصم بالبغاء بقاعدة الاستصحاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary's statement is not astonishment like Zachariah's, since he wanted a child while she feared and rejected this outcome; the later Aal Imran account could omit the additional denial of prostitution.
rows.anchor: لاختلاف الحالين لأن حال زكرياء حال راغب في حصول الولد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: بغي is a feminine term for an adulterous woman without the feminine هاء; Ibn Ashur explains its form through the root بغي and assimilation of the resulting consonants.
rows.anchor: والبغي : اسم للمرأة الزانية ، ولذلك لم تتصل به هاء التأنيث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angel answers in effect that Mary's concern is true, but redirects her request into a wise explanation that this creation is easy for God.
rows.anchor: وجواب الملك معناه : أن الأمر كما قلت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feared social injury to Mary is not great beside God's purpose of guiding people through Jesus; public benefit takes precedence over an individual's private interest.
rows.anchor: لأن مراعاة المصالح العامة تقدم على مراعاة المصالح الخاصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here هو refers to the harm implied in Mary's words about not having a husband or being a prostitute, unlike Zachariah's case where it refers to the child's creation; the angel speaks for God, but the answer is attributed to the angel because he directly answers Mary.
rows.anchor: فضمير { هو علي هين } عائد إلى ما تضمنه حوارها من لحاق الضر بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ولنجعله continues the angel's account of God's sending and gift: the child is an honor to Mary, while his being a sign and mercy honors the child, with a shift into God's first-person voice.
rows.anchor: وقوله { ولنجعله } عطف على { فأرسلنا إليها روحنا } باعتبار ما في ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: وكان أمرا مقضيا may still be the angel's speech or a new sentence; its pronoun refers to the promised gift, and the statement ends Mary's appeal because conception has already occurred.
rows.anchor: وجملة { وكان أمرا مقضيا } يجوز أن تكون من قول الملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ف marks the consequence and close succession: Mary conceived immediately after the exchange; حملت means conception, while حملت به adds the sense of close attachment, illustrated by Abu Kabir al-Hudhali's poetry.
rows.anchor: الفاء للتفريع والتعقيب ، أي فحملت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: قصيا means far from her family; the word derives from distance and the passage gives no reason to specify a particular place.
rows.anchor: و { قصيا } بعيدا ، أي بعيدا عن مكان أهلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An account that Mary fled to Egypt, helped by Yusuf the carpenter, and gave birth there is incorrect; Luke places the birth at Bethlehem in Judea, consistent with her later return to her people carrying Jesus.
rows.anchor: قيل : خرجت إلى البلاد المصرية فارة من قومها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Labor followed the completed pregnancy in ordinary sequence; one report says it began after eight months.
rows.anchor: للتعقيب العرفي ، أي جاءها المخاض بعد تمام مدة الحمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أجاءها derives from جاء with causative hamza, then metaphorically means forcing her to come to a place; al-Farra notes this Arabic use, also found in a proverb and Zuhayr's verse.
rows.anchor: معناه ألجأها ، وأصله جاء ، عدي بالهمزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: المخاض means labor, the fetus's movement toward birth; the جذع is the palm's main trunk between roots and branches, where Mary leaned.
rows.anchor: والمخاص بفتح الميم : } طلق الحامل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one calling Mary is the baby she carried; the phrase من تحتها can mean from beneath her, or use من as a relative pronoun for the boy below her. The latter reading makes the newborn's speech a sign of Jesus and an honor to Mary.
rows.anchor: ضمير الرفع المستتر في ( ناداها ) عائد إلى ما عاد عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Readers differ in parsing من تحتها: Nafi, Hamza, al-Kisai, Hafs, Abu Jafar, Khalaf, and Ruh read من as a preposition; Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, Ibn Amir, Abu Bakr, and Ruways read it as a relative pronoun for the child.
rows.anchor: قرأ نافع ، وحمزة ، والكسائي ، وحفص ، وأبو جعفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Specifying that the baby called from beneath her depicts him speaking as soon as he was born, before she lifted him, to comfort her at once and portray the intimate moment of birth.
rows.anchor: ولإفادة أنه ناداها عند وضعه قبل أن ترفعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أنلا is explanatory of the call; the statement about the stream explains why Mary should not grieve, since her circumstances merit joy as a divine honor.
rows.anchor: خبر مراد به التعليل لجملة { ألا تحزني }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: سريا means a flowing stream; God provides pleasant food and drink as a visible honor and evidence of her innocence to Yusuf the carpenter and any witnesses. Water nearby and fresh dates out of season from a dead palm would be extraordinary; fresh fruit is more appealing than dried dates.
rows.anchor: السري : الجدول من الماء كالساقية ، كثير الماء الجاري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shaking the dry palm trunk brings out fresh dates by God's blessing, another miracle and a visible honor that strengthens Mary's certainty.
rows.anchor: أن يكون إثمار الجذع اليابس رطبا ببركة تحريكها إياه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The باء in بجذع intensifies contact; وهزي includes the meaning of bringing near, so Mary draws the trunk toward herself. The reflexive subject and object are acceptable despite grammarians' caution, as in 28:32.
rows.anchor: وضمن { وهزي } معنى قربي أو أدني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: رطب is partly dried dates, and جني means freshly picked, implying they have just fallen and were not stored; fruit newly fallen from the tree tastes better.
rows.anchor: والجني : فعيل بمعنى مفعول ، أي مجتنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most readers pronounce تساقط with open تاء and doubled سين; Hamza lightens it by deleting a تاء, Hafs uses ساقطت to make the palm drop its fruit, and Yaqub reads يَسَّاقَط with the trunk as subject.
rows.anchor: و { تساقط } قرأه الجمهور بفتح التاء وتشديد السين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The instructions to eat, drink, and be comforted summarize the preceding provisions; قرّة عين is a multi-step metaphor for joy from the opposite expression for weeping, and includes comfort, happiness in the baby, assurance of his safety, and his future distinction.
rows.anchor: وقرة العين : كناية عن السرور بطريق المضادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The قاف in قري is open because it is the present tense of قررت عينه, with assimilation and vowel transfer.
rows.anchor: وفتح القاف في { وقري عينا } لأنه مضارع قررت عينه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The baby continues speaking with God's revelation to Mary: vow a fast and stop speaking to avoid debate, remain in worship, and rest from ignorant questioning.
rows.anchor: هذا من بقية ما ناداها به عيسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Silence was worship in earlier religious laws and pre-Islamic Arab practice, including a mute pilgrim; Islam abrogated it, while a man named Abu Israel was told to speak, take shade, sit, and complete only his fast.
rows.anchor: وكان الانقطاع عن الكلام من ضروب العبادة في بعض الشرائع السالفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Bakr told a woman who had vowed silence that Islam had abolished this practice and she should speak; the account of the silent woman pilgrim likewise attests to the earlier custom.
rows.anchor: وروي عن أبي بكر الصديق رضي الله عنه أنه دخل على امرأة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary's قول is a gesture indicating her vow; if fasting required silence, one sign sufficed, but if these were separate vows she signaled each separately. She knew the infant would answer, as shown by her pointing to him later.
rows.anchor: وأطلق القول على ما يدل على ما في النفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In ترين, the emphatic نون follows deletion of the indicative نون under the conditional particle, and the ياء takes a matching vowel.
rows.anchor: والنون في قوله { ترين } نون التوكيد الشديدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إنسي means a human individual, formed with a relational ياء from the collective noun إنس; its indefinite form after negation means no person, and the rhyme does not imply an exception for angels.
rows.anchor: والإنسي : الإنسان ، والياء فيه للنسب إلى الإنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary came to her people after Jesus had finished speaking; Luke's forty-one-day interval after childbirth shows that the ف can mark customary, not immediate, sequence.
rows.anchor: دلت الفاء على أن مريم جاءت أهلها عقب انتهاء الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Her people are residents of her locality; carrying Jesus openly shows she did not conceal him, trusting God to clear her of suspicion.
rows.anchor: وهذه الحال للدلالة على أنها أتت معلنة به غير ساترة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their statement is a fresh explanatory exchange and rebuke; فري most likely means an atrocious deed, as Mujahid and al-Suddi say, associating the word with a false claim about a child of adultery.
rows.anchor: وأظهر محامله هنا أنه الشنيع في السوء ، قاله مجاهد والسدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some linguists instead derive الفريّة from أفرى, cutting skin to ruin or burn it, distinguishing it from فرى without hamza, which means cutting to repair.
rows.anchor: ومن أهل اللغة من قال : إن الفري والفرية مشتقان من الإفراء بالهمز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Arab usage, a woman may be called the sister of a tribal ancestor's descendants; this reading takes Mary as descended from Aaron.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن معنى { ياأخت هارون } أنها إحدى النساء من ذرية هارون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Ashur rejects interpreters' claim that Mary descended from Solomon; he identifies her family with Aaron's line.
rows.anchor: وما وقع للمفسرين في نسب مريم أنها من نسل سليمان بن داوود خطأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Luke's genealogy likewise makes Elizabeth, Zachariah's wife and Mary's cousin, a descendant of Aaron.
rows.anchor: وامرأته من بنات هارون واسمها إليصابات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran may compress both senses of the phrase without contradicting the Mughirah report; the genealogical reading is distinct from the preferred literal-sibling reading.
rows.anchor: ولعل قومها تكلموا باللفظين فحكاه القرآن بما يصلح لهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: امرأ سوء means a man whose deeds cause harm; her people imply that her conduct is foreign to her parents' character, praising them in the wording while accusing her of unprecedented immorality.
rows.anchor: وعنوا بهذا الكلام الكناية عن كونها أتت بأمر ليس من شأن أهلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary's gesture directs the people to ask the infant or hear his answer; because the gesture functions as a reply, their following words are narrated as a separate utterance.
rows.anchor: أي أشارت إليه إشارة دلت على أنها تحيلهم عليه ليسألوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their question is a denial both of an infant's ability to speak and of Mary's directing them to him; they challenge either expecting an answer or putting a question to him.
rows.anchor: والاستفهام : إنكار ؛ أنكروا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The extra كان in من كان في المهد emphasizes the infant's established state in the cradle and intensifies their incredulity; زائد is usually expressed in the past tense.
rows.anchor: وزيادة فعل الكون في { من كان في المهد } للدلالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: في المهد is the predicate of the relative pronoun من; صبيا is its circumstantial accusative, and المهد means an infant's bed or prepared cradle.
rows.anchor: وقوله { في المهد } خبر ( من ) الموصولة
